title: Rapid Pilot Conversion Cheatpack (Engineer-first) - WIP
content:
Purpose
- One-page field-play cheatpack for sellers + SEs to convert engineering pilots inside 48–72 hours.
- Engineer-first language, minimal product marketing. Focus: prove latency+cost SLOs, safe fallbacks, and measurable success criteria.

Target audience
- Platform/infra engineers evaluating inference (internal platform teams, ISVs, fintech, regulated SaaS).
- Typical ask: 3–5 day pilot, integration with small dataset, SLA/throughput ramp.

TL;DR (30s engineer pitch)
- We provide a drop-in inference endpoint (hosted or private) that matches your latency SLO with predictable cost.
- Pilot plan: sample integration + 1k real calls/day or replay of 100k tokens; we show latency & cost delta vs baseline in 48h.

30s business pitch (for buyer exec)
- Fast proof of value: measurable reduction in per-response latency variance and clear per-token cost visibility. Pilot shows production economics before commit.

Key win criteria (explicit, measurable)
- Latency: p95 < customer-SLO (usually 300–600ms) for the pilot workload
- Cost: projected per-1000-token cost within agreed threshold (+/- 15%)
- Reliability: <1% error rate, transparent fallbacks configured
- Integration: SDK or REST call in CI test suite (sends recorded requests)

Pilot plan (48–72h cheat)
Day 0 (pre-call)
- Quick checklist: API key, region, model choice (we recommend an efficient variant), sample prompt set, baseline metrics collected by customer (latency, cost)
- Preflight: ask for a 1–2 minute recording of the endpoint behavior (postman/curl examples) or a small replay dataset (CSV/JSON).
Day 1 (integration)
- Provide minimal SDK snippet (Python/Node) and a reference test harness to replay requests.
- Configure continuous batching + prefix caching if prompts share prefixes. Turn on streaming only if client supports it.
- Start 1k synthetic calls (mirror their traffic distribution). Capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, error codes.
Day 2 (analysis & ramp)
- Run 100% replay of 1–10k real requests if available. Share dashboard: token breakdown, hot-token cost, KV cache hit rate.
- Demo results: show delta vs baseline and recommend config changes (quantization, batch size, model variant).

Quick technical scripts (copy-paste)
- Python snippet (minimal):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key="REDACTED", region="us-west-2")
  resp = c.generate(model="efficient-llama-7b-8k", prompt=my_prompt, max_tokens=200)
  print(resp.latency_ms, resp.token_cost)
- Curl health check:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

Rapid config knobs to mention (and why)
- Model variant: cheaper quantized variant for throughput-critical flows (explain small accuracy vs cost tradeoff)
- Batching: increases throughput, slightly higher tail latency — recommended for async pipelines
- KV/prefix caching: huge win for repeated or templated prompts (show %cost reduction examples)
- Function/tool calling: disable during latency-critical tests to avoid plumbing overhead

Standard objections + suggested responses
- "We can't expose data to hosted cloud": Offer private deployment & VPC option; provide KMS/HSM integration checklist and audit log sample.
- "We need predictable latency": Propose dedicated pool or reserved capacity pilot + predefined autoscale floor. Include canary timeout config and fallback to lighter model.
- "Costs look higher than our in-house GPU": Reframe as unit economics: include ops savings (no ops team), improved utilization via batching/caching, and predictable pricing in multi-region. Provide a TCO snapshot template.

Demo flow (10 min)
1) Quick setup (1 min) — show SDK auth and health check
2) Baseline replay (3 min) — run a short replay and surface p95/p50, token counts
3) Live tweak (3 min) — flip batching/cache and re-run small batch to show immediate impact
4) Economics (2 min) — projected per-1k-token cost, cache hit effect, and fallback plan

Handoff to eng after pilot
- Deliverables we provide: traffic replay file, SLO report, recommended runtime config (JSON), SLA statement (draft), rollout checklist for canary->gradual->full.
- Handoff note template to platform team (short):
  - pilot-id: REDW-PL-XXXX
  - model: efficient-llama-7b-8k (quantized)
  - suggested autoscale: min 2 pods, max 10; fallback: smaller 3b model
  - known caveats: streaming disabled, tool-calls disabled

Pricing & negotiation levers to offer in pilot
- Time-limited discounted reserved capacity for pilot week (15% off)
- Free first 100k tokens for verification, then usage metered
- Option to convert pilot usage to reserved commit with uplift credit for early sign-up

Competitor triggers (what to listen for)
- If buyer mentions "we already run on VendorX with bespoke infra" -> emphasize integration delta & observability (per-route tracing + token-level cost).
- If buyer pushes on "model ownership" -> emphasize serving economics, fallback policies, and multi-model routing.

Security / compliance quick notes
- For regulated customers: propose private control plane + HSM key wrap; outline a short data flow diagram in follow-up.
- Offer SOC2 artefacts and sample audit log export (note: attach after NDA).

One-pagers / assets to attach to email
- 1-page: Pilot SLO template (we provide)
- 1-page: Quick config cheat (batching/caching/quantization explained in bullets)
- Mini-dashboard snapshot (png) showing p95 and token-cost breakdown (mock example)

Sample outreach snippets (short)
- Email subject: "48h pilot to prove latency + cost for inference"
- Opening line: "We can run a 48–72h pilot using a replay of your traffic and show p95 latency, token-cost, and fallback plan — no infra changes required."
- Follow-up ask: "Can you share a 1k-sample of requests or a replay file by EOD? I’ll send an SDK snippet to get you going.

Open decisions / notes to self
- Need a clipped TCO template that compares: VendorX on-prem, self-hosted GPU, Redwood-hosted w/ caching.
- Confirm legal artifact flow for private deployment pilots (Rina owns).
- Build a tiny pilot dashboard template (Liam) that auto-populates from pilot logs.

Attachables / next steps checklist for SE
- [ ] Create pilot workspace + API key (label: <acct>-pilot-<date>)
- [ ] Send SDK snippet + replay harness
- [ ] Kick off 1k synthetic calls and validate health
- [ ] Schedule 30-min results walk-through (Day 2)

Notes to self (tone: raw, internal)
- Keep scripts minimal. Sellers will drop non-essential steps. Focus on observable wins: p95 and cost.
- Avoid deep model-limit explanations in first demo — saves time.
- Make sure to have fallback story ready: "If tail latency spikes, we’ll route to a smaller variant and retry with exponential backoff."

Appendix: example metrics to show (copyable)
- p50,p95,p99 latency (ms)
- token_count, token_cost (USD)
- cache_hit_rate (%)
- batching_utilization (%)
- error_rate (%)

End 
- This is a living cheatpack. Keep feedback from field: short debrief note after each pilot is gold.
